promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Commercialisation of sport and the media
Ethical and socio-cultural issues (drugs and violence)

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised social/personal factor affecting participation rates in physical activity?
questions.explain: Gender is one of the key factors (alongside age, socio-economic group, ethnicity and disability) that affects participation.

questions.q: Which of these is a barrier to participation rather than a strategy to increase it?
questions.explain: A lack of disposable income is a barrier, while the other options are strategies used to overcome barriers.

questions.q: Why might a lack of positive role models reduce participation among a particular social group?
options: People are less likely to see the sport as achievable or relevant to them
It directly reduces the number of pitches available
It increases the cost of equipment
It makes officials biased against them
questions.explain: Visible role models help people identify with a sport and believe participation is realistic for them.

questions.q: A community offers women-only swimming sessions. Which barrier is this strategy most directly trying to overcome?
options: Cultural or religious concerns about mixed-sex activity
Lack of transport to the pool
questions.explain: Single-sex sessions address cultural/religious barriers that may discourage some groups from mixed-sex activity.

questions.q: A sports club wants to raise participation among older adults on low incomes. Which combination best targets their specific barriers?
options: Concessionary pricing and off-peak daytime sessions
questions.explain: Reduced pricing tackles the income barrier and daytime sessions suit retired people, addressing both barriers together.

questions.q: Which statement best explains how disability can affect participation?
options: A lack of accessible facilities and specialist coaching can limit opportunities
Disabled people are not allowed to compete in any sport
It only affects participation in team sports
It has no measurable effect on participation levels
questions.explain: Inaccessible facilities and shortage of appropriate coaching or adapted equipment are recognised barriers for disabled people.

questions.q: The 'golden triangle' describes the interdependent relationship between sport and which two other elements?
questions.explain: The golden triangle links sport, the media and sponsorship/business, each relying on the others.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised type of sponsorship?
questions.explain: Sponsorship types include financial, and clothing/equipment or facilities, provided in return for advertising.

questions.q: Which of these is a form of media used to cover sport?
questions.explain: Media forms include television, radio, print (newspapers/magazines), the internet and social media.

questions.q: How does commercialisation typically benefit a professional performer?
options: It provides income allowing them to train full-time
It reduces the amount of media coverage they receive
It removes the need for sponsors
It lowers spectator interest in their sport
questions.explain: Sponsorship and media income allow performers to become full-time professionals and focus on training.

questions.q: Which is a negative effect of commercialisation on a sport?
options: Sponsors and media can pressure sports to change rules or timings
It removes all funding from grassroots sport
It always reduces the audience for the sport
It bans the use of technology
questions.explain: Sports may alter rules, formats or event timings to suit sponsors and broadcasters, a recognised drawback.

questions.q: Why can increased media coverage be a negative for spectators watching at a venue?
options: Events may be scheduled at inconvenient times to suit TV audiences
It reduces the number of players on the pitch
It removes the need for officials
It makes tickets free of charge
questions.explain: Kick-off times are often set to maximise TV viewers rather than to suit attending spectators.

questions.q: A drinks company pays a tennis player to wear its logo and appear in adverts. This is best described as which relationship?
options: Sponsorship of a performer by a business
questions.explain: A business paying a performer for advertising and endorsement is a classic sponsorship arrangement.

questions.q: A broadcaster introduces frequent advert breaks and slow-motion replays during a match. Which effect of commercialisation does this best illustrate?
options: The media changing the way a sport is presented
A reduction in the sport's funding
questions.explain: Advert breaks and replays show how media coverage reshapes the presentation and experience of sport.

questions.q: Playing within the rules and spirit of a game, showing respect to opponents, is best described as:
questions.explain: Sportsmanship is competing fairly, within the rules and spirit of the game, with respect for others.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of gamesmanship rather than sportsmanship?
options: Time-wasting to gain an advantage while staying within the rules
Kicking the ball out so an injured player can be treated
Shaking hands with opponents after the match
Applauding a good play by the opposition
questions.explain: Gamesmanship uses methods that stretch the rules or spirit of the game to gain an advantage without breaking the letter of the law.

questions.q: Which performance-enhancing drug increases red blood cell count to improve oxygen delivery for endurance events?
questions.explain: EPO stimulates red blood cell production, increasing oxygen transport and benefiting endurance performance.

questions.q: Which type of drug is most associated with steadying nerves and reducing heart rate in sports such as archery and shooting?
questions.explain: Beta blockers reduce heart rate and anxiety, steadying the hands for precision sports.

questions.q: Why do some power athletes use anabolic steroids?
options: They increase muscle mass and allow more intense training
They reduce heart rate before competition
They mask the presence of other drugs
They improve oxygen-carrying capacity for endurance
questions.explain: Anabolic steroids promote muscle growth and faster recovery, allowing harder, more frequent training for strength/power athletes.

questions.q: A boxer needs to lose weight rapidly to make a lower weight category and also wants to dilute a banned substance in their urine. Which drug type would they most likely misuse?
questions.explain: Diuretics increase urine output for rapid weight loss and can dilute or mask other banned substances in a sample.
